newsitem.title: USA: NYC might not get tax surcharge extended -- paper.
newsitem.headline: NYC might not get tax surcharge extended -- paper.

text.p: Talks between Democratic New York State lawmakers and New York City over extending the city's personal income tax surcharge broke down late Monday in a dispute over how the funds would be spent, the New York Times said in its Tuesday edition.
New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, a Republican, has said he wants any legislation extending the tax to give him more flexibility over using the money.

But the Assembly Speaker, Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, said he wanted written assurances from the mayor that he would use a substantial share of the money to hire more police officers. The 12.5 percent surcharge, which helped pay for 6,000 new police officers, expires on December 31 unless the state legislature extends it.
The legislature on Tuesday will begin a special session, which Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, has predicted could be as short as one day.
The paper quoted Gov. George Pataki as saying "I think it's unlikely that we will reach agreement," after he met with legislative leaders late Tuesday.
